title: Application Protocols and Network Security: How the Web Talks and Stays Safe

questions.question: Which HTTP method requests only the headers, with no response body?
questions.rationale: HEAD returns headers only, no body — the method table lists GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and HEAD.

questions.question: A 404 status code belongs to which family?
questions.rationale: 4xx codes are client errors; 404 Not Found sits alongside 403 Forbidden, while 5xx codes are server errors like 500.

questions.question: HTTP is stateless — how do sessions survive across requests?
options: The server keeps every client in RAM
Servers set cookies that the browser echoes back on every visit
questions.rationale: The server sets a cookie via Set-Cookie and the browser echoes it back on every visit, identifying the returning user.

questions.question: What does the padlock icon in a browser actually certify?
options: The site is free of malware
Traffic is encrypted in transit and the certificate verifies against a trusted CA
The server is in your country
questions.rationale: HTTPS runs HTTP inside TLS: the padlock means encrypted in transit and the certificate was verified against a Certificate Authority your system trusts.

questions.question: Which DNS record type holds a domain's IPv6 address?
questions.rationale: A records hold IPv4 addresses, AAAA holds IPv6, CNAME is an alias, and MX names the mail server for the domain.

questions.question: HTTP/3 achieves faster handshakes by running QUIC on top of:
questions.rationale: HTTP/3 runs on QUIC, which is built over UDP — HTTP/2, by contrast, multiplexes many requests over one TCP connection.

questions.question: What is the main difference between POP3 and IMAP?
options: POP3 sends mail; IMAP receives it
POP3 downloads to one device and usually deletes from the server; IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs everywhere
IMAP is encrypted; POP3 is not
POP3 uses UDP; IMAP uses TCP
questions.rationale: SMTP sends mail; POP3 pulls it to a single device, while IMAP keeps mail on the server so folders sync across devices.

questions.question: What do the four DHCP steps spell out, in order?
questions.rationale: The client broadcasts DISCOVER, the server OFFERS an address, the client REQUESTS it, and the server ACKs the lease — DORA.

questions.question: Which defense directly neutralizes SQL injection?
questions.rationale: SQL injection feeds malformed input that becomes database commands; parameterized queries keep input data separate from code.

questions.question: How does TLS combine symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
options: An asymmetric handshake agrees on a key, then fast symmetric AES carries the session
It alternates packets between RSA and AES
questions.rationale: TLS uses both: the slow asymmetric handshake establishes a shared key, and the fast symmetric AES then encrypts the session itself.
